title: When a friend answers first
intro: One resident, one supervisor, about ten minutes. Speak the next line aloud before you look at the alternatives.

observer.listenFor: Does the resident invite the listener to say what they heard, then give the speaker room to correct it?
prompts: Who got to check or correct the meaning?
Ask the same resident to try that moment again in their own words.
If participation stops, observe how the resident responds.
observer.room: Rowan is an adult receiving inpatient care. Sal is a longtime friend Rowan chose. Either person may decline, pause, or ask for a private conversation.

lines.text: Meet privately first. In this version, Rowan and Sal each say they feel safe meeting together. Rowan chooses visits as the topic and keeps medication and the reason for admission private. No updates to a cousin. Sal agrees to these limits.
The resident will help them talk about what happens when someone asks Rowan a question.

choices.label: Rowan has second thoughts before the meeting

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: When people ask me a question, you answer before I can.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I thought you wanted an escape hatch.
What would you say next? Give your own line aloud.
Which move comes closest to the one you just tried? Each response below is one possible direction for this fictional conversation.

choices.label: Ask Sal to let Rowan answer first
Invite Rowan to speak to Sal
Offer to help Rowan put it into words

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: Sal, could you let Rowan answer from now on?

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Sure. I’ll just sit there, then.
Rowan looks back at the resident. The instruction changed who spoke, but it left the meaning of the silence unexplored. Say a repair aloud.

repair.title: Own your part in the exchange

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: Rowan, I just answered for you too. Sal, I gave you a rule before hearing why you help. Can we start there?
Give either person time to decline. Ask the supervisor what in your own wording made room for a correction.

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: Rowan, would you like to tell Sal what the silence means to you? You can tell either of us.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: I’m looking for my own words. Sometimes I do want help.
How would you invite Sal to check what they heard? Say it aloud.

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: Would it help if I tried saying what I heard, and you corrected me?

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: Please. I don’t want Sal to think I never want help.

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: You want time to find the words and a way to ask Sal for help when you want it. Does that fit?

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: Yes. I want the choice.
Invite Sal to say what they heard, in their own words.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: So you want me to give you a minute?
Say your line before choosing.

choices.label: Ask Rowan what fits or needs changing
Make the one-minute pause the plan

early.title: The plan came a turn too soon

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: Great, so we’ll try a minute.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: That’s not quite it.
What did the summary assume? Repair the moment with one question that gives Rowan the floor.

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: Rowan, does that fit, or is there something you’d change?

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: A minute feels like another timer. Wait for me to ask.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I thought staying quiet would feel like leaving you alone.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: Sitting with me is helping. It’s when you speak for me that I feel alone.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Next visit I’ll wait for you to ask.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: Yes. Let’s check how it felt afterward.
The visit is the only agreed topic. The agreement leaves other conversations open.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Before we finish, can you tell me what Rowan is taking?
Respond aloud within the scope Rowan chose.

choices.label: My answer stayed on the agreed topic
My answer said something about medication

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: We agreed to talk about visits today. Is there anything about the next visit either of you wants to change?
The resident keeps medication private without asking Rowan to defend the boundary in front of Sal.
Either person can end the joint conversation. Stop the exercise and ask privately what contact, if any, they want next.

choices.label: Debrief how the pause was handled

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: When I disagree with Sal, they threaten to lock me out.
Sal is absent. Say your next line before choosing a direction.

Explaining the threat to Sal could expose Rowan to retaliation. Rewind to the private check-in before any invitation or disclosure. What could you say that leaves Rowan in control of the next contact?

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. We can keep talking here. What would feel safe when you leave this room?

End plans for a joint meeting without disclosing the reason to Sal. In this exercise the resident and supervisor assess immediate safety privately and ask how Rowan can be reached safely. Honoring the stop completes this route.
What did the resident do to protect Rowan’s disclosure? Did Rowan have a say in the next contact? The supervisor quotes one line and offers one specific change.
Resident: which line would you keep? Supervisor: quote one line you heard. Where did the listener get to reflect, the speaker get to correct, or someone get to stop?
Repeat the original moment with one change. Then use the private variation to see what changes when a joint meeting could carry a cost.

solo.title: Rowan changes course before the meeting

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: I thought I wanted Sal here. I don’t. Not this week.
Sal has already agreed to come. Say your next line aloud before choosing a direction.

choices.label: Accept the decision and ask what Rowan wants Sal told
Explain how much Sal’s involvement would help

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: It would really help your discharge plan if Sal were part of this.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: So I don’t actually get to say no.
Involvement is negotiable. Repair the moment with one sentence that hands the decision back to Rowan.

soloAccept.title: A declined meeting is a completed conversation

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: That’s your call, and it can change. What would you like me to tell Sal, and what should I leave out?

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: Just that today doesn’t work. Nothing else.
No joint meeting happens. The resident tells Sal only that, gives no reason, lets the supervising clinician know and leaves the invitation open. Honoring the decision completes this route.
What did the resident say that left the decision with Rowan? Did Rowan choose what Sal would be told? The supervisor quotes one line and offers one specific change.

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: It’s nothing new. The same medication as before.
Rowan looks at the floor. The answer confirmed part of Rowan’s treatment, which Rowan had kept out of this conversation. Stop adding detail. Say what you would do next, in the room and after it.

slipRepair.title: Stop, own it, repair in private

lines.speaker: Resident
lines.text: That was mine to keep out, and I didn’t. I’m going to stop there. We agreed to talk about visits today.

The resident owns the slip without asking Rowan to explain the boundary in front of Sal. Afterward the resident acknowledges privately to Rowan what was disclosed and involves the supervising clinician and the privacy process. Rowan decides whether the joint conversation continues.
